full_judgment:
2. The relevant facts necessary for the disposal of this Civil Appeal are in a mutshell, that the predecessor of the respondents No.1(a)-1(g), Md Rafiquzzaman Bhuiyan as plaintiff filed the Other Class Suit No.201 of 1980 on 12-11-1980 for declaration of title over "Kha' schedule land and later on after amendment prayed for recovery of Khas possession by evicting the defendants No. 8-10 from the suit land as appended to the plaint stating, inter alia, that the father of plaintiff Md Rafiquzzaman Bhuiyan and the pro-forma defendants No.2-6, namely Alhaj Ali Azam purchased 0.22 acres of land by Kabala dated 10-2-1953 from Kailash Chandra Bhuiyan, Khetra Mohan Bhuiyan and Botu Keshar Bhuiyan in the Benami of pro-forma defendant No.7. Said Alhaj Ali Azam died leaving behind the plaintiff Md Rafiquzzaman Bhuiyan and the pro-forma defendants No.2-6 as sons and daughters. The plaintiff got the suit "Kha' schedule land by amicable partition with pro-forma defendants No. 2-6 and since the date of Kabala the plaintiff has been possessing the suit land. On 1240-1980 the plaintiff came to know that the suit land has been recorded in Khas Khatian in the name of the defendant No. l. The defendant No.1 is trying to lease out the suit land. By a subsequent amendment to the plaint the plaintiff further claimed that during the pendency of the suit the defendants No.8-10 forcibly entered into the suit land on 18-11-1980 and constructed a tin-shed structure although they were not entitled to enter into or construct any house in the suit land. 

 3. The government as defendant No.1 contested the said suit by filing written statement, contending, inter alia, that the suit land is government Khas land and is part of the Bazar namely Zamindar Hat. The said land has been recorded in Khas Khatian No.1 during SA and MRR operation, All the Bazars became khas land and were vested to the government from 1st Baishak 1368 BS as per The State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and the government has been leasing out the said Bazar since 1368 BS Accordingly during preparation of MRR Kkatian the same has been recorded as Hat in the name of the Government, The plaintiff never possessed the suit land and, as such, he has no right, title or interest over the suit land, hence the suit is liable to be dismissed. The suit land is being possessed by the defendant No. 7, who constructed a grocery shop thereon and subsequently applied for lease of the Suit land.
